Task: Classify crop types using NDVI time series
Classify agricultural land cover types (paddy, palm, coconut, others) by computing NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data across multiple bi-monthly periods between March and August 2022, generating a stacked NDVI image used as input for Random Forest classification, with accuracy assessment and export of the classified cropland map.

Task: Smooth NDVI time series
Compute a smoothed annual NDVI time series from 2013 to 2020 using Savitzky-Golay filtering on mean NDVI images. It first fills missing values in the image collection by interpolating neighboring years, then applies temporal smoothing to reduce noise and reconstruct a consistent NDVI trajectory. The output includes both the original and smoothed NDVI layers, as well as Land Productivity Dynamics Index (LPD) maps derived before and after smoothing for land degradation assessment.

Task: Analyze annual temperature extremes
Calculate and visualizes mean annual maximum and minimum temperatures for Central American countries and the Dominican Republic using TerraClimate data from 2018. It computes regional averages via reduceRegion, generates histograms of temperature distributions, and creates time series charts of monthly min/max temperatures from 2000 to 2020. Outputs include printed statistics, histograms, and interactive charts showing thermal patterns over time and space.

Task: Extract vegetation and moisture indices
Compute multiple spectral indices (NDSI, NDVI, NBR, QNIR_SSWIR, QLSWIR_NIR, QLSWIR_SSWIR) from a mosaicked Landsat 5 TM image collected in summer 2004 over a specific WRS path/row region. It generates a composite index stack (StackVI) and exports both the original reflectance mosaic (CropLandsatVer) and the derived spectral index stack to Google Drive at 30m resolution clipped to a user-defined area (AreaTrabajo).

Task: Classify land cover in positive and negative segments
Classify land cover in segmented regions derived from Landsat surface reflectance imagery using Random Forest classification. It processes four temporal segments (SEG_01 to SEG_04), separates pixels into positive and negative magnitude classes based on band 'b5', applies thresholds on spectral bands (b3, b4, b5) to isolate specific conditions, trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled samples (DF_SGx, BE_SGx, DD_SGx, Reg_SG2), and produces classified raster outputs for each segment. The final output includes multiple classified maps such as 'Segmento_1_Positivo_ClaRF' and exports one of the filtered segmentation results ('SEGM_04_Negat300final') to Google Drive.

Task: Classify agricultural and natural land cover
Classify land cover types in a rural area using Sentinel-2 imagery from August 2018. It trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled sample regions (classesLagoa) using spectral features from the median composite (B11, B8, B4). The output is a classified raster map with four classes—'Área Plantio', 'Solo', 'Vegetação Natural', 'Agua'—and an area statistics table showing pixel count, hectares, and percentage per class. The classification result is exported to Google Drive, and a legend is added to the map for visualization.

Task: Identify vegetation anomaly periods
Analyze MODIS NDVI time series from 2000 to 2020 over Argentina to compute a historical baseline of NDVI values and their standard deviation for each 16-day period. It then evaluates the 2020 NDVI data across nine consecutive 16-day intervals, calculates z-score anomalies by comparing current conditions with the historical mean and standard deviation, and classifies areas with significant negative anomalies (below -0.52 standard deviations) as anomalous. These classified anomalies are stacked into a multi-band image and summed to produce a final frequency map showing how many times each pixel experienced anomalous vegetation decline during January–May 2020. The output is a single-band summary raster visualized with a custom color palette and exported to Google Drive.

Task: Calculate vegetation indices and coverage fraction
Calculate multiple vegetation indices (RVI, NDVI, EVI, PSRI, WDRVI, SIPI, AFRI, SAVI, MSAVI, MSAVI_af) from Landsat 5 surface reflectance data, derives fractional vegetation cover (FC) from MSAVI_af, and exports zonal statistics for these indices over sample regions. It also visualizes the results on the map and exports the MSAVI image to Google Drive.

Task: Compute annual NDVI composite
Calculate the annual mean NDVI composite for the Heihe River Basin using MODIS MCD43A4 data for the years 2019 and 2020. It processes monthly NDVI images, clips them to the study area, computes maximum-value composites per month, then averages all months to produce an annual mean NDVI image for each year. The resulting images are exported to Google Drive.

Task: Map land surface changes over time
Generate median composite images from multiple Landsat and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance datasets across five time periods (2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020) to visualize and export land surface changes. It applies sensor-specific cloud masking functions (for Landsat 4–8 and Sentinel-2) to improve data quality, computes median pixel values within each period, clips to a region of interest (roi), and visualizes the results using a near-infrared false-color composite (B4, B5, B3). Outputs include layered maps for visualization and five separate GeoTIFF exports of the median composites at 30m resolution for change analysis.

Task: Estimate forest fuel moisture
Estimate Live Fuel Moisture Content (LFMC) in forested areas using MODIS MOD09A1 surface reflectance data. It computes the Visible Atmospherically Resistant Index (VARI) from red, green, and NIR bands, normalizes it between seasonal min/max extremes (RVARI), and applies an empirical exponential equation to derive LFMC. A fire history mask excludes recently burned areas (within 5 years), and a forest mask based on tree cover (>10% from Hansen dataset) restricts output to woody vegetation. Monthly composites (2005–2020) are generated, and for each month (Jan, Feb, Aug–Dec), pixel-wise maximum, minimum, and 10th/30th/70th/90th percentiles of LFMC are exported as rasters clipped to the East_Bioreg region.

Task: Analyze vegetation health and coverage
Calculate multiple vegetation indices (RVI, NDVI, EVI, PSRI, WDRVI, SIPI, AFRI, SAVI, MSAVI, MSAVI_af) from Landsat 5 surface reflectance data to assess vegetation condition and fractional canopy cover within the Juruti project area. It exports index values averaged over sample regions and visualizes outputs including a fractional cover map derived from MSAVI_af.

Task: Extract wind speed over time
Extract hourly wind speed data (Wind_f_inst) from the GLDAS NOAH model for January 2012, computes daily mean wind speed images, combines them into a multi-band image representing each day of the month, clips the result to the Khuzestan region, and exports the final 31-band raster to Google Drive. The output is a spatiotemporal stack of daily average wind speed over Khuzestan for January 2012.

Task: Estimate water surface area and volume using NDWI
Calculate water surface area or reservoir volume over time using multiple NDWI-based indices derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, applying cloud masking and spatial clipping to a user-defined geometry. Outputs are printed as comma-separated values for each date, including results from up to five different NDWI formulations.

Task: Map monthly surface water extent
Analyze surface water dynamics in the Varahanadhi Basin, Tamil Nadu, using Sentinel-2 imagery from January to December 2018. It computes NDWI for each month, applies dynamic thresholds to classify water pixels, masks non-water areas, and calculates monthly water surface area in square kilometers. The output includes a time-series of monthly water extent maps, binary water masks, and a printed list of monthly water areas for hydrological analysis.

Task: Estimate vegetation cover fraction
Calculate multiple vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, MSAVI, MSAVI_af) from Landsat 5 TOA data over the Juruti project area for September 2011, derives a Fraction of Cover (FC) from MSAVI_af, and exports both the index values and FC as images and regional statistics to Google Drive. It also performs spectral unmixing to estimate land cover fractions.

Task: Calculate daily heat stress index
Calculate a daily Heat Stress (RRI) index for the year 2018 using meteorological variables derived from GLDAS data. It first aggregates hourly temperature, humidity, pressure, solar radiation, wind speed, and mean temperature into daily max, min, and mean values. Then, it computes relative humidity from specific humidity and surface pressure, and finally applies a linear expression to derive the RRI index. The output is a single mean image of the daily RRI index over the global land area (excluding masked regions), exported at 25 km resolution.

Task: Generate true color composite
Generate a median true-color composite image from Landsat surface reflectance data over a specified latitude-longitude bounding box and seasonal period (June to September). It selects specific decades (1970s, 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, or 2010s) based on the 'decade' parameter, applies cloud masking appropriate to the satellite sensor (Landsat 1 MSS, Landsat 5 TM, or Landsat 8 OLI), and composites up to five years of imagery. The output is a visually interpretable RGB image displayed in Earth Engine, using band combinations appropriate for each sensor (e.g., B4/B3/B2 for Landsat 8), with map centering over the defined spatial extent.

Task: Estimate mean evapotranspiration over time
Calculate the long-term mean evapotranspiration (ET) from MODIS MOD16A2 data for consecutive hydrological years (September to May) between 2001 and 2018, then computes the overall mean ET across all these periods. The final output is a single image representing the average ET over the entire 17-year span, exported to Google Drive for multiple spatial regions.

Task: Analyze surface water extent using MSI
Analyze surface water extent in the Donnelly region across multiple years (1988, 2011, 2017–2021) using the Moisture Stress Index (MSI) derived from Landsat surface reflectance imagery. It applies sensor-specific cloud masking functions (cloudMaskL457 for Landsat 4–5 and maskL8sr for Landsat 8) to filter poor-quality pixels, computes median composites per time period, calculates MSI as the ratio of shortwave infrared to near-infrared bands, and visualizes the results using a color palette to indicate varying moisture levels. Outputs include masked, clipped true-color images and MSI layers mapped over the study area for comparative temporal analysis.

Task: Extract nighttime light intensity
Extract DMSP-OLS nighttime stable lights imagery for a specified country from 1992 to 2013. It loads annual stable_lights bands from multiple satellite-year combinations (F10, F12, F14, F15, F16, F18), clips each image to the country boundary, and exports them individually to Google Drive at 1000m resolution. Outputs are georeferenced raster files named by ISO code and satellite-year (e.g., tza_dmspols_F101992), enabling spatiotemporal analysis of urbanization and human activity.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, computing NDVI and applying an SVM classifier trained on labeled ground truth points for seven classes: Paddy, WaterBody, Forest, Builtup, Rubber, Coconut, and Barrenland. The output is a classified raster map with distinct color coding for each land cover type and a confusion matrix to assess training accuracy.

Task: Generate annual mosaic composites
Generate and visualizes annual mosaic composites for Ecuador in 2021 and 2022 using Landsat 8, Landsat 9, and unspecified 'ly' satellite data, focusing on the Amazon and Pacific regions with median SWIR1, NIR, and red bands for visualization.

Task: Identify burned areas in subhumid forest
Identify and maps burned areas within the subhumid deciduous forest of Chiquitania by analyzing MODIS MCD64A1 fire data from 2000 to 2020, applying uncertainty filtering (≤25), temporal segmentation, masking, and vectorization to extract persistent fire-affected regions not overlapping with prior burns.

Task: Calculate daily heat stress index
Calculate a daily Heat Stress Index (ETI) for the year 2018 using meteorological variables derived from GLDAS data. It processes hourly temperature, humidity, wind speed, pressure, and radiation data to compute daily max, min, and mean air temperatures, then derives relative humidity and applies a biophysical expression to estimate ETI. The final output is a single mean ETI image representing average daily heat stress conditions across the globe for 2018, exported at 25 km resolution.

Task: Identify crop cultivation area
Identify crop cultivation areas using NDVI derived from Sentinel-2A/B Surface Reflectance imagery collected between July and October 2021. It processes biweekly image collections by computing NDVI, generating greenest pixel composites via qualityMosaic, and applying a cloud mask based on blue band reflectance (B2 < 2500). A crop mask is created by detecting persistent vegetation (NDVI ≥ 0.2) across six consecutive biweekly periods. The output includes a binary crop area raster map, a time-series chart of mean NDVI over the region, and a stacked NDVI composite for visualization, all masked using a land use layer (pb_mask.eq(40)).

Task: Analyze NDVI time series trends
Analyze long-term NDVI time series from multiple Landsat sensors (5, 7, and 8) over two specific sites—PN Conguillío and I La Fusta—in Temuco, Chile. It computes linear and harmonic regression models to characterize vegetation dynamics, detrends the NDVI series, and generates fitted seasonal curves. Outputs include charts of raw NDVI, detrended NDVI, and harmonically fitted NDVI for both locations.

Task: Extract district boundary geometry
Extract the geometric boundary of specific districts in Nepal (MYAGDI, KASKI, SYANGJA, TANAHU, GORKHA, MANANG, MUSTANG, PARBAT, BAGLUNG, LAMJUNG) from a user-uploaded feature collection. It filters the FeatureCollection by DISTRICT attribute to isolate each district's geometry, with the final assigned 'boundary' variable corresponding to the last defined district (LAMJUNG). the workflow prints the resulting geometry and displays only the KASKI district boundary on the map in red color.

Task: Calculate daily climate index
Calculate a Climate Condition Index (CCI) using meteorological variables from the CFSV2 model. It processes daily maximum temperature, specific humidity, surface pressure, downward short-wave radiation, and wind components to derive relative humidity and wind speed, then combines them into a composite CCI through empirical expressions. The final output is a mean CCI image over the specified date range, exported to Google Drive and visualized on the map with a custom color palette.

Task: Analyze nighttime light intensity per administrative unit
Calculate the sum of stable nighttime lights from 1992 to 2013 within each administrative boundary defined in a feature collection. It processes a time series of DMSP-OLS stable lights images, masks values below 6, and uses reduceRegion to compute total NTL values per polygon. The output is a FeatureCollection with added NTL sums and area for each unit, exported to Drive.

Task: Calculate heat stress days
Calculate daily heat stress conditions in 2016 using meteorological variables from the CFSV2 reanalysis dataset. It derives temperature, humidity, wind speed, solar radiation, and atmospheric pressure to compute multiple thermal comfort indices (THI, THIadj, CCI), applies a threshold (THIadj > 68) to identify heat stress days, and accumulates consecutive days of exceedance into a final raster map representing total heat stress days for the year. The output is exported as a single-band image at 30 km resolution covering global latitudes from -60° to 80°.

Task: Monitor fire-affected area
Analyze Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data before and after the Proenca-a-nova wildfire event in September–October 2020 to generate median composite images for visual assessment of burn areas and post-fire recovery using shortwave infrared, near-infrared, and red bands (B12, B8, B4).

Task: Extract land fraction by CRMS site
Extract the percentage of land cover (Perc_Land_Fin) from a time-series of Landsat-derived fractional land images for each CRMS (Coastal Reference Monitoring System) site, generating a feature collection with mean land fraction values per site per year, and exports the results to a CSV file.

Task: Analyze NO2 emissions over regions
Analyze nitrogen dioxide (NO2) column number density over seven geographical regions of Turkey (Marmara, Ege, Akdeniz, Doğu Anadolu, Güneydoğu Anadolu, İç Anadolu, Karadeniz) using Sentinel-5P satellite data for the same 19-day period (April 29 to May 17) across 2019, 2020, and 2021. It generates time-series charts showing daily average NO2 levels per year for each region, enabling comparison of air quality trends during these years.

Task: Map land cover change over time
Visualize annual Landsat mosaic images from 2006 to 2017 clipped to a specific region in South America, and overlays 21 validation vector layers likely representing different land cover classes or reference samples for accuracy assessment. The primary purpose is to analyze temporal land cover changes using multi-year composites and validate results against ground truth data.

Task: Estimate nighttime light intensity per postal code
Calculate calibrated nighttime light intensities for a series of years (1992–2012) using DMSP-OLS stable lights data. It applies sensor-specific calibration equations to correct for inter-sensor variability, clips values to the valid range (0–63), and aggregates the annual calibrated nighttime light values within each postal code boundary using zonal statistics. The output is a CSV table exported to Google Drive containing summed nighttime light values and area for each postal code.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types in the TESE region using Sentinel-2 imagery from July 2016. It computes a median composite for the month, then applies a Random Forest classifier trained on sample regions (classesLagoa) with features derived from Sentinel-2 bands (B11, B8, B4). The classification distinguishes four classes: Área Plantio, Solo, Vegetação Natural, and Agua. The output is a classified raster map displayed with a custom palette and exported to Google Drive, along with a legend added to the map interface.

Task: Analyze vegetation and water trends
Analyze temporal trends in vegetation and surface water conditions using Landsat surface reflectance data from 1984 to 2018, computing NDVI and LSWI indices over specific Arctic regions. It generates median composites for summer months (July–August) within selected years (1984–1986, 1998–1999, 2018–2019), masks clouds and shadows, and visualizes long-term greening, browning, and stable trends across different periods (1984–1999, 1984–2015, 1984–2018, 2000–2015, 2000–2018).

Task: Classify agricultural cultivation area
Classify agricultural cultivation areas using 12 temporally consecutive Sentinel-2 SR images from October 2021 to March 2022. It computes NDVI for each bi-monthly period, creates a cloud-free composite using qualityMosaic('NDVI'), and stacks the resulting NDVI bands into a multitemporal image. A Random Forest classifier is trained on user-defined training regions (cultivo and otros) to classify cultivated areas. The output includes a classified raster map (masked to class 1), an estimated cultivation area in hectares, a temporal NDVI profile chart by class, and an accuracy assessment via confusion matrix. An interactive NDVI time series chart is also enabled on map click.

Task: Detect land cover change
Detect land surface disturbance using LandTrendr algorithm on Landsat and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from 1984 to 2019. It applies cloud masking to Landsat 7, Landsat 8, and Sentinel-2 collections, computes median composites for visualization across multiple years, and runs a time-series segmentation to identify changes in spectral trajectories. The primary output is a change map showing magnitude and year of detection, which is clipped, classified by magnitude thresholds, and exported as a raster. Additionally, the change metrics are sampled at specific point locations (CAM_2017 and DEF_2017_2018_2019) and exported as a shapefile for validation or further analysis.

Task: Extract fractional land cover over time
Extract yearly fractional land cover (specifically 'Init_Land') from Landsat MSS data between 1973 and 1985 for the Bayou Perot and Bayou Rigolettes region, computes mean values per year within the specified watershed boundaries, and exports the results as a CSV file summarizing temporal land fraction changes.

Task: Sum hourly precipitation rates
Calculate the cumulative sum of hourly precipitation rates from GSMaP data over a 24-hour period spanning two consecutive days, specifically from 07:00 on 2018-11-26 to 06:00 on 2018-11-27, clipped to a predefined region 'mo'. The output is a single image representing total accumulated precipitation over that interval.

Task: Compute mean evapotranspiration over time
Calculate the mean evapotranspiration (ET) from MODIS MOD16A2 data for consecutive hydrological years (September to May) between 2001 and 2018, creates a time series of annual mean ET images, computes the long-term average across the entire period, and exports the results as image files to Google Drive for multiple regions. It also prints metadata about the image collections.

Task: Analyze land surface temperature
Analyze land surface temperature (LST) dynamics over a specific region using MODIS LST Day data from May 2014 to April 2015. It processes seven temporal phases of MOD11A1 imagery, converts digital values to Celsius by multiplying by 0.02 and subtracting 273.15, preserves image timestamps, and generates DOY (day-of-year) time series charts of mean LST for each phase using region-based reduction over a user-defined feature collection. Outputs are seven interactive charts showing temporal LST patterns across the study area.

Task: Extract land fraction in wetlands
Calculate the percentage of land cover within historically possible wetland areas across the Gulf of Mexico from 1985 to 2020, using a time series of fractional land images derived from Landsat data. It masks these images to wetland areas and aggregates the results by hydrologic unit (HUC-10) basins, exporting the mean land percentage per basin per year as a CSV file.

Task: Monitor reservoir water area using NDWI
Calculate water surface area over time using multiple spectral indices (EVI, NDPI, NDVI, SAVI, NDWI, NDTI) derived from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, with a focus on NDWI for water detection. It processes images day-by-day within a user-defined date range, masks clouds, applies scaling factors, and computes the mean NDWI value within a geometry to estimate water extent. Outputs include daily area measurements for different indices.

Task: Classify land cover using Sentinel-2
Classify land cover in the TESE region using a Random Forest classifier trained on Sentinel-2 imagery from July 2016. It uses a feature space derived from median-composited Sentinel-2 bands (B11, B8, B4) and training samples from a separate image collection over the rural area (Lagoa) in 2019. The classification produces a map with four classes: Área Plantio, Solo, Vegetação Natural, and Agua. The output includes a classified raster map visualized with a legend, exported to Google Drive, along with intermediate mosaics of monthly Sentinel-2 composites for 2016.

Task: Analyze absorbing aerosol index
Analyze the Absorbing Aerosol Index (AAI) from Sentinel-5P data over seven geographical regions in Turkey (Marmara, Aegean, Akdeniz, Doğu Anadolu, Güneydoğu Anadolu, İç Anadolu, and Karadeniz) for the period April 29 to May 17 across 2019–2021. It generates time-series charts showing daily mean AAI values per year for each region, focusing on atmospheric aerosol loading and its interannual variation.

Task: Analyze NDVI changes over time
Compute and visualizes NDVI composites from Landsat 8 imagery across eight consecutive 16-day periods over East Java (Jawa Timur) in 2017, generating time-series vegetation health maps and calculating mean NDVI values for the region in each period.

Task: Extract NDVI values for bioregions
Extract mean NDVI values from MODIS MOD13Q1 for specific bioregions (CLC_BIOREGION) in the Mediterranean region (BRG='MED') for years 2005–2013, and for all regions in 2004, using spatial reduction to compute pixel statistics within vector features. The output is a CSV file containing BRG, CLC, YEAR, imageId, and mean NDVI values.

Task: Identify water area from NDWI
Identify water extent in the AREA_DAN region using NDWI derived from Landsat imagery (Landsat 5 and Landsat 7) for two time periods: a base condition (2006–2019) and a flooded condition (2001–2019). It computes NDWI using band ratios, applies a threshold to classify water pixels, masks non-water areas, calculates total water surface area in hectares within the study polygon, and outputs raster layers for water presence, mosaicked composites, and tabulated area statistics. Visualizations include base and flooded mosaics, water masks, and administrative boundaries.

Task: Classify urban land expansion
Classify urban land expansion over time by creating a training dataset from point samples labeled as 'urban' across 35 years (1986–2020), using Landsat surface reflectance data. It computes NDVI and NDWI indices, fits a temporal model using a linear trend (with time variable 't'), and prepares annual median composites for change detection in the region of interest.

Task: Classify land cover using NDVI time series
Classify land cover types (Crop, Noncrop, Water, BU) using a time-series of fortnightly NDVI composites derived from Landsat 8 TOA data. It computes NDVI for 12 bi-monthly periods, creates a stacked NDVI image, trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled regions, and produces a classified land cover map with accuracy assessment. Outputs include the classified map, confusion matrices, overall accuracy metrics, and a temporal NDVI profile chart by class.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover into multiple classes (agriculture, urban, wetlands, mangroves, dunes, forests, water bodies, etc.) using a Random Forest classifier trained on spectral indices and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2015. The output is a classified land cover map with accuracy assessment including confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and producer/consumer accuracies.

Task: Analyze NDVI time series
Compute and stacks NDVI values from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data across eight 15-day intervals between July and October 2021, generating a composite image for temporal vegetation analysis. It masks pixels based on blue band thresholds and exports a scaled, masked NDVI stack for regional monitoring.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover in the TESE region using Sentinel-2 imagery from July 2016. It constructs a feature space from median-composited Sentinel-2 bands (B11, B8, B4), trains a Random Forest classifier using training samples ('classesLagoa') on a separate image from June 2016 over the 'rural' area, and applies the model to classify four classes: Cultivated Area, Soil, Natural Vegetation, and Water. The output is a classified raster map displayed with a custom legend and exported to Google Drive, along with visualizations of monthly mosaics from January to December 2016.

Task: Detect fire activity using thermal bands
Identify fire activity by analyzing thermal infrared data from Sentinel-2 and FIRMS datasets, visualizing burned areas and active fires in the Sumapaz region and surrounding points of interest between February 2020 and December 2020, with a focus on cloud-filtered imagery for accurate detection.

Task: Extract Landsat imagery over Guatemala
Filter and retrieves multiple Landsat image collections (Landsat 1–5) within a specific date range and spatial extent over Guatemala. It defines a study area using a country boundary from the USDOS/LSIB_SIMPLE dataset, applies temporal and spatial filters to each Landsat collection, and prints the resulting image counts. It also visualizes one composite layer (L5) and includes additional layers for Argentina for comparison. The primary output is filtered ImageCollections for different Landsat missions, intended for land surface analysis over time.

Task: Sum nighttime light by postal area
Calculate the total nighttime light radiance from VIIRS DNB monthly composite imagery over a multi-year period (2012–2016) within defined postal regions. It loads and combines 57 monthly 'avg_rad' images into a single multiband image, then uses reduceRegion with a sum reducer to compute the cumulative radiance for each postal feature at 1000m scale. The result is a FeatureCollection where each postal unit contains summed NTL values across all months and its area, which is printed, visualized, and exported as a table.

Task: Classify agricultural areas using NDVI time series
Classify agricultural land use in the Bikaner district by analyzing a time-series of scaled NDVI values derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It computes fortnightly greenest pixel composites, builds a stacked NDVI image, trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled regions, performs classification, and evaluates accuracy using validation data. Outputs include classified maps, area statistics in square meters, training and validation accuracy metrics, and a temporal NDVI profile chart across 12 fortnightly periods.

Task: Extract fractional land cover over time
Extract the percentage of land cover (Perc_Land_Fin) from a series of precomputed Landsat-derived fractional images for the Gulf of Mexico region, specifically within the Bayou Perot and Bayou Rigolettes area, and exports the mean values per polygon per year as a CSV file. The output includes annual and sub-annual (pre/post) observations from 1985 to 2020.

Task: Extract wind speed over time
Extract hourly wind speed data (Wind_f_inst) from the GLDAS NOAH model for January 2012, computes daily mean wind speed images by reducing each day's observations, and compiles them into a multi-band image representing 31 days of wind speed. The final output is clipped to the Khuzestan region and exported to Google Drive as a raster dataset named 'Month_01_Khuzestan_wind_366'.

Task: Classify agricultural areas using NDVI time series
Generate a land cover classification map focusing on agriculture by computing NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a 6-month period (October 2021–March 2022). It divides the timeline into 12 bi-monthly intervals, computes the greenest pixel composite using qualityMosaic('NDVI'), stacks the resulting NDVI images, scales the values, and applies a Random Forest classifier trained on user-provided labels ('crop' and 'other') to produce a classified raster identifying agricultural areas. The output includes a false-color visualization of stacked NDVI composites and a masked classification result highlighting class 1 (likely cropland), which is added to the map for visual interpretation.

Task: Extract nighttime light intensity
Extract nighttime light radiance values over a user-defined area of interest (AOI) using VIIRS DNB monthly composite imagery from 2009 to 2023. It specifically selects and clips the 'avg_rad' band for six specific months (April 2012, April 2014, April 2016, April 2018, April 2020, and January 2022) to analyze temporal changes in nighttime light intensity. The output includes six clipped images exported to Google Drive, each representing the average radiance at night for Bangkok or the AOI, visualized with a fixed stretch (0–60), enabling urbanization or electrification trend analysis.

Task: Generate true-color composite image
Generate a median true-color composite image from Landsat surface reflectance data for a specified spatial and temporal window. It selects the appropriate Landsat satellite (Landsat 1, 5, or 8) based on the input year, applies sensor-specific cloud masking, computes the median pixel value across the image collection, and visualizes the result in true color (RGB). For Landsat 8, bands B4, B3, and B2 are used; for Landsat 5, bands B3, B2, and B1; and for Landsat 1, bands B4, B5, and B6. The output is displayed on the map as a visual layer with appropriate stretch and gain settings.

Task: Analyze CO emissions trend
Analyze the temporal variation of carbon monoxide (CO) column number density over seven geographical regions in Turkey (Marmara, Aegean, Mediterranean, Eastern Anatolia, Southeastern Anatolia, Central Anatolia, and Black Sea) using Sentinel-5P satellite data for the period April 29 to May 17 across 2019, 2020, and 2021. It generates yearly daily-of-year (DOY) line charts showing mean CO concentrations within each region, aiming to compare interannual air quality patterns during this specific spring window.

Task: Analyze land fraction change over time
Calculate and exports the mean percentage of land cover within HUC-10 watersheds using yearly fractional land images from 1985 to 2020, with a focus on wetland-associated regions in the Gulf of Mexico. The output is a CSV file containing per-basin annual land fractions.

Task: Analyze NDVI temporal changes
Compute and visualizes NDVI composites from Landsat 8 imagery over East Java (Jawa Timur) across eight consecutive 16-day periods between June and October 2019, generating mean NDVI values for the region to analyze vegetation dynamics over time.

Task: Classify crop types using NDVI time series
Classify agricultural land cover types (paddy, palm, coconut, others) by computing NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data across eight 15-day intervals between November 2022 and February 2023, generating a multi-band NDVI composite for supervised classification using CART, and evaluating accuracy with training and validation datasets.

Task: Compute mean evapotranspiration over time
Calculate the long-term mean evapotranspiration (ET) from MODIS MOD16A2 data by first computing annual mean ET images for consecutive hydrological years (September to May), then combining them into a multi-year mean image representing the average ET from 2001 to 2018. The final output is exported to Google Drive for multiple spatial regions.

Task: Classify fire management zones
Classify post-fire vegetation recovery zones in a specific region using a combination of slope, aspect, and NBRR (Normalized Burn Ratio Recovery) indices. It computes a weighted index from clipped slope and aspect layers derived from SRTM and multiplies them with NBRR, then applies Random Forest classification trained on user-provided training points. The resulting classified raster is segmented into vector polygons for two management zones (Zona_G and Zona_NG), each labeled with management type (1 or 2) and class ID (1–18), producing two merged feature collections representing managed and non-managed areas for spatial analysis.

Task: Analyze ozone concentration trends

Task: Estimate vegetation fraction using spectral unmixing

Calculate water surface coverage using multiple NDWI-based indices (A to E) from Sentinel-2 data, applying cloud masking and spatial clipping. It outputs daily water extent as area (km²) or volume (via external volume function) over a user-defined date range and region, printing results for each valid image date.

Task: Classify land cover using Random Forest
Classify land cover types (Degradation, Deforestation, Forest, Non-Forest, Regenerated Non-Forest) using a Random Forest classifier applied to a multi-temporal Landsat surface reflectance stack. It trains the model using labeled polygons (Degradacion, Deforestacion1, etc.), evaluates band importance, and outputs a classified raster map (DD1_DD2_DF_NBRrg) along with a variable importance chart for feature interpretation.

Task: Generate monthly Sentinel-2 mosaics
Generate monthly median composites of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over the TESE region for the year 2016. It filters images by date and boundary, applies a cloud filter (with <30% cloud cover in September), computes median pixel values per month, clips to the study area, and visualizes each composite using SWIR (B11), NIR (B8), and red (B4) bands. It also exports one of the composites (February collection, July mosaic) to Google Drive as a GeoTIFF for further analysis.

Task: Map marshland extent over time
Map the spatial extent of marshlands annually from 1986 to 2020 using Landsat surface reflectance data, applying NDVI and NDWI for vegetation and water detection, with manual polygon feature collections representing marsh areas for each year.

Task: Classify forest areas using satellite imagery
Classify forested areas in Malawi using Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data by applying NDVI, NDWI, and BSI indices, performing cloud masking, and training a classifier on labeled points. It generates two forest classification maps (from Landsat and Sentinel) and evaluates them using validation points. Median, mean, 20th percentile, and standard deviation composites are created for temporal analysis across multiple years.

Task: Monitor drought conditions using NDVI and LST
Compute multiple drought indices by analyzing MODIS Terra (MOD09GA) surface reflectance and Aqua (MYD11A1) land surface temperature data over a dynamic 30-day window ending five days before the current date. It calculates long-term mean, max, min, and standard deviation of NDVI and LST from historical data (2002–previous year), then compares current-year values to derive standardized anomalies: NDVI-Z-index, VCI, TCI, VHI, and combined drought index (NDVI+LST-AN). The workflow includes cloud masking, water/land masking, snow masking, and pixel observation filtering. Outputs include mapped layers for VCI, TCI, VHI, NDVI-Z-index, LST-Z-index, and snow cover, visualized with red-to-green color palettes indicating drought severity.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types using a random forest classifier trained on Landsat 8 imagery from April 2015 to March 2018 over Tsukuba, Japan. It generates classified maps and evaluates accuracy using training and validation datasets, with outputs including confusion matrices, overall accuracy, and GeoTIFF exports of leaf-on, leaf-off composites, and the final classified image.

Task: Detect land cover change
Detect land cover changes using LandTrendr algorithm applied to Landsat surface reflectance imagery from 1984 to 2019 over a user-defined area (geometry9). It computes a change map based on spectral index B5 (SWIR1), identifying the magnitude and year of detection of significant changes. The output includes two visual layers: 'Magnitude of Change' and 'Year of Detection', with additional visualization of Sentinel-2 and Landsat composites for 2016–2018, and overlays a feature collection (CAM_2017) for reference.

Task: Classify land cover using Random Forest
Classify land cover in the Vichada and Amazonas regions of Colombia using a time series of filtered segmentation images derived from Landsat data. It applies mask-based filtering to retain valid change detection segments, merges training samples from two areas, builds a Random Forest classifier using temporal spectral features (startVal, endVal, mag) across four time segments, and classifies a combined image stack covering both regions. The output is a classified land cover map which is clipped and exported to Google Drive.

Task: Analyze methane tillage and rainfall change
the workflow dynamically calculates change indicator values for methane, tillage, and rainfall between user-specified dates at selected agricultural sites in California. It generates time series charts and visualizations using Sentinel-5P, Sentinel-2, and CHIRPS datasets, with interactive map outputs showing site-specific changes.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types in the Maqu Basin using Sentinel-2 imagery and auxiliary environmental variables. It computes spectral indices (NDWI, MNDWI, NDVI, LSWI), combines them with topographic (slope, aspect, relief, TWI), climatic (precipitation, temperature), and hydrological layers, then applies a Random Forest classifier trained on sample points to generate a land cover classification map. Outputs include the classified image, variable importance chart, accuracy assessments (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, kappa), and exported results to Google Drive.

Task: Estimate vegetation cover fraction
Calculate multiple vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, MSAVI, MSAVI_af) from Landsat 5 TOA reflectance data, computes a Fraction of Cover (FC) from MSAVI_af, and exports both the index values and FC to CSV files for sample regions. It also visualizes spectral unmixing and various vegetation/soil/water indices.

Task: Extract surface water using MNDWI
Compute the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) using green and SWIR bands from Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance data to identify surface water extent across multiple years, with specific visualization and analysis focused on the year 2011. The output includes masked composite images and MNDWI layers for annual time steps, primarily used for monitoring surface water dynamics.

Task: Classify land cover types using Landsat imagery
Classify land cover types in a specified region using Landsat 5 surface reflectance imagery from 2003 and 2004. It computes spectral indices (NBR, QNIR_SSWIR, QLSWIR_NIR, QLSWIR_SSWIR, NDVI) for both winter and summer seasons, merges multi-path/row scenes via mosaicking, and trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled training sites (e.g., forest, shrubland, urban, water). The classification is performed on a composite image with multiple spectral and derived bands, and the output is a classified raster map of land cover types exported to Google Drive, along with visualization on the map.

Task: Estimate vegetation cover using MSAVI
Calculate multiple vegetation indices (RVI, NDVI, EVI, PSRI, WDRVI, SIPI, BRI, CVI, GLI, NDRE, LCI, AFRI, CCCI, CRE, NDMI, SAVI, MSAVI, MSAVI_af) from Sentinel-2 data over the Brasília National Park for the period June–September 2018. It computes a fractional vegetation cover (FC) from MSAVI_af and exports zonal statistics of all indices to CSV files based on sample plots. Additionally, it visualizes the composite image, boundaries, and selected indices on the map.

Task: Calculate vegetation indices for sample areas
Calculate multiple vegetation and land surface indices (RVI, NDVI, EVI, PSRI, WDRVI, SIPI, BRI, CVI, GLI, NDRE, LCI, AFRI, CCCI, CRE, NDMI, SAVI, MSAVI, MSAVI_af, FC) from Sentinel-2 imagery over a specific region and time period. It then extracts mean values of these indices for sample polygons (amostras) and exports the results as CSV files to Google Drive. Additionally, it visualizes the indices and region boundaries on the map.

Task: Generate WaSSI hydrologic model inputs
the workflow prepares geospatial input datasets required by the WaSSI (Water Supply Stress Index) hydrologic model, specifically for the USA. It assembles and harmonizes 8-day LAI time series (2000–2020), long-term monthly LAI climatology, impervious surface fractions (USA and Mexico), and SAC-SMA soil parameter maps (uztwm, uzfwm, uzk, zperc, rexp, lztwm, lzfsm, lzfpm, lzsk, lzpk, pfree). It also exports utility functions for zonal statistics — including band-wise zonal means (zonalImg), time-series zonal reduction (zonalTS), watershed rasterization (RasterizeWS), band-to-image-collection conversion (bandToCollection), and land-cover-stratified LAI aggregation (zonalGroupLAI) — enabling watershed-scale extraction of biophysical and soil properties for hydrologic modeling.

Task: Map land cover change
Visualize annual Landsat mosaic images from 2006 to 2017 clipped to a region of interest and overlays 21 validation vector layers, likely representing different land cover classes or validation samples over time, to support land cover change analysis. The output includes mapped imagery layers for each year and vector overlays for comparison, with an export function to download the 2017 mosaic.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types using a Random Forest classifier trained on multispectral satellite imagery and auxiliary geospatial layers. It computes spectral indices (NDVI, SAVI), texture features (GLCM contrast, entropy), topographic attributes (slope, elevation), and soil properties (clay, sand, AWC, etc.) as predictors. Training samples are extracted via stratified sampling based on a reference land cover map (Target), and the model's accuracy is validated using a confusion matrix and overall accuracy. The output includes a classified land cover map, training/testing partitions, and accuracy assessment metrics.

Task: Detect illicit farm growth
Analyze a time series of Landsat 7 false color (B5/B4/B3) images to detect the construction, growth, and destruction of an illicit marijuana farm in northern Mexico. It computes band differences (specifically B4) between a baseline image (March 8, 2011) and subsequent images, classifies vegetation change using mean and standard deviation thresholds, estimates cultivated area in acres via pixel counting within an AOI, and outputs a time-series chart of plantation area. A slider-controlled visualization allows interactive exploration of the site's evolution, with dynamic labels describing each stage.

Task: Classify agricultural land cover
Classify paddy, palm, and coconut cultivation areas using a time series of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It computes NDVI for 12 bi-monthly periods, creates a composite image stack, and applies a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions to generate a land cover map.

Task: Extract terrain variables for inselberg points
Extract multiple terrain indices (CTI, TRI, slope, VRM, roughness, TPI, SPI) from the Geomorpho90m dataset within a user-defined polygon area intersecting national boundaries. It clips these layers to the intersection of the input polygon and relevant countries, then performs spatial lookup of terrain values at specified inselberg point locations. The output includes a median composite of CTI for visualization and prepares terrain variable extraction at point locations for further analysis.

Task: Extract nighttime light intensity
Analyze nighttime light (NTL) intensity in the AOI using VIIRS DNB monthly composite imagery from 2012 to 2022. It extracts specific monthly images at fixed timestamps, selects the 'avg_rad' band representing average radiance, clips them to the study area, and exports each clipped image to Google Drive. The visualization uses a fixed stretch (0–60) for display, and outputs include six individual GeoTIFFs of NTL for different years.

Task: Compute NDVI for dry and rainy seasons
Calculate the mean Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for two distinct time periods in 1985 (January–May and July–October) using Landsat 5 Surface Reflectance data, masked for clouds, and clipped to a user-defined geometry from a Fusion Table. It also retrieves and prints metadata of specific Landsat 5 images filtered by WRS path and row for further inspection.

Task: Detect forest loss fragmentation
Analyze forest loss patterns in Laos using the Geary's C spatial autocorrelation statistic derived from differenced forest cover data (2014–2018) in the UMD Hansen global forest change dataset. It computes year-specific forest loss (2014–2018) and calculates changes between 'first' and 'last' observation years for multiple canopy cover thresholds. The primary output is a clipped, masked raster of Geary's C values for the 2018 forest loss within the 2016–2018 version of the dataset, focusing on the diff_b40 band, which reflects structural changes in forest cover at 40% canopy density. This highlights spatial clustering or dispersion of forest loss, indicating fragmentation patterns.

Task: Identify tidal flat areas
Identify tidal flat areas by creating a training dataset from point samples labeled as 'tidal_flat' across multiple years (1986–2020), filtering them within a region of interest, and exporting the collection to an asset. It also prepares annual median surface reflectance images from Landsat 5, 7, and 8 for visualization and potential classification input.

Task: Analyze NDVI over time
Analyze vegetation dynamics using NDVI derived from Sentinel-2 images on four specific dates in January and February 2020, applying cloud masking with SCL-based masks and temporal compositing to generate comparable NDVI maps. Outputs include NDVI visualizations for each date and a time series chart of mean NDVI at a point location.

Task: Classify tree cover using Sentinel and Landsat
Classify forest areas by applying a random forest model to gap-filled median composites of Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data from 2018–2020, using training points for five land cover classes. It exports classified tree cover maps and aggregated tree cover sums per region for accuracy assessment.

Task: Classify post-event land cover
Classify land cover types after an event (likely a fire or deforestation) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from September 2021. It trains a Random Forest classifier with manually labeled training polygons for seven classes—agricultural area, water, two forest types, bare soil, other, and burned area—and applies it to generate a classified land cover map.

Task: Identify jute cultivation area using NDVI
Identify jute cultivation areas in the Darrang district of Assam, India, using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from April to June 2022. It computes NDVI for six bi-weekly periods, applies quality mosaicking (greenest pixel), masks non-agricultural areas and low-reflectance pixels, scales and clips the results, and exports a bi-weekly NDVI image (specifically scaled_ndvi2) for further analysis. The output includes mapped layers with custom color palettes for NDVI thresholds and an export task for a classified NDVI raster.

Task: Classify crop types using NDVI time series
Classify cropland types (paddy, palm, coconut, others) by computing NDVI from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data across multiple bi-monthly periods in 2022, generating a stacked NDVI image used to train and validate a CART classifier, resulting in a land cover classification map and accuracy assessment.

Task: Summarize nighttime light intensity per postcode
Calculate the sum of stable nighttime lights from 1992 to 2013 within each postcode boundary. It uses a series of DMSP-OLS stable_lights images, combines them into a multi-band image, masks values below 6, and then computes the zonal sum for each feature in the input postcode FeatureCollection using reduceRegion with a sum reducer. The output is a FeatureCollection where each postcode has attributes for the summed nighttime light values across all years and its area, which is exported to Google Drive.

Task: Analyze NDWI and NDVI for rainy season
Analyze vegetation and water conditions over a specified geometry during multiple rainy seasons (2019–2022) using Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data. It computes NDVI, NDWI, and BSI indices, applies cloud masking using QA60 band for Sentinel-2 and a custom cloud removal function for Landsat 8, then aggregates the time series by calculating median, mean, 20th percentile, and standard deviation for optical and index bands. The output is a gap-filled composite image per sensor, clipped to the study area, with visualizations for true color and index-based maps (e.g., NDWI_mean), displayed in a split-panel interface comparing Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 results.

Task: Generate monthly Sentinel-2 mosaics
Generate monthly median composites of Sentinel-2 imagery over the BIGUA region for the entire year of 2016. It filters images by date and boundary, computes median pixel values across each month's collection, clips to the study area, and visualizes the result using a false-color composite (SWIR/NIR/Red: B11/B8/B4). For September, an additional cloud cover filter (less than 30% cloudy pixels) is applied. The outputs include 12 monthly mosaicked images added to the map and printed lists of image acquisition dates for each month, enabling temporal analysis of surface reflectance.

Task: Estimate vegetation cover using MSAVI
Calculate multiple vegetation indices (RVI, NDVI, EVI, PSRI, WDRVI, SIPI, BRI, CVI, GLI, NDRE, LCI, AFRI, CCCI, CRE, NDMI, SAVI, MSAVI, MSAVI_af) from Sentinel-2 data over the Brasília National Park for the period June–September 2018. It computes median composites, clips to the park and sample plot boundaries, visualizes indices, and extracts mean values within sample plots for export. The final output includes a fractional vegetation cover map derived from MSAVI_af, along with CSV exports of all index means per sample plot and a GeoTIFF export of the MSAVI image.

Task: Identify cropland distribution
Identify cropland areas in Liaoning using NDVI time series derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data for 2020, 2021, and 2022. It computes monthly greenest-pixel composites based on NDVI, stacks the monthly NDVI bands scaled to uint8, and applies a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled crop and non-crop samples to classify cropland. The classification is masked to retain only predicted cropland (class 1), and results are exported as 10m resolution GeoTIFFs to Google Drive. Accuracy assessment is performed using validation samples, including error matrices and overall accuracy. A temporal NDVI profile chart across months is also generated for training regions.

Task: Map land cover change over time
Create mean composite images from multiple Landsat and Sentinel-2 collections over Guyana for five-year intervals (2000–2005, 2005–2010, 2010–2015, 2015–2020) using surface reflectance data, applies scaling factors, masks clouds, and visualizes SWIR-based false-color composites to analyze temporal changes in land cover, particularly focusing on vegetation, moisture, and surface conditions.

Task: Classify land cover in Amazon and Vichada
Classify land cover in the Colombian departments of Vichada and a merged Amazon region (including Arauca, Casanare, Meta, Guainía, Vaupés, Amazonas, Guaviare, Putumayo, and Caquetá) using time-series segmentation images derived from Landsat. It applies mask filtering based on classification layers, merges multi-temporal segments (SEG01–SEG04), builds a composite image stack of change metrics (startVal, endVal, mag), and trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled training data (Landcover classes). The final output is a classified land cover map over the combined area, which is clipped and exported to Google Drive.

Task: Classify land cover using segmentation and RF
Classify land cover in the VICHADA department of Colombia using a time-series segmentation approach combined with Random Forest classification. It processes four segmented images (SEG01 to SEG04) derived from Landsat data, masks them using positive and negative classification layers, and creates a composite image stack with attributes 'startVal', 'endVal', and 'mag' for each segment. A Random Forest classifier is trained on labeled samples from 'Entrebamiento_RF_' feature collection using these attributes, and applied to generate a classified land cover map. Additionally, annual median surface reflectance composites from Landsat 7 and 8 are generated for temporal analysis from 2000 to 2019, which are likely used for change detection or contextual validation.

Task: Analyze nighttime light intensity per postal code
Analyze calibrated nighttime light intensity across different years within administrative boundaries defined by a feature collection of postal codes in Thailand. It loads and calibrates DMSP-OLS stable lights imagery from 1992 to 2012 using quadratic regression models specific to each satellite-year, clips values to the valid range (0–63), and aggregates the sum of calibrated stable lights for each postal code polygon using reduceRegion. The output is a CSV table exported to Google Drive containing summed nighttime light values and area for each postal code.

Task: Summarize nighttime light intensity per postal code
Analyze calibrated DMSP-OLS nighttime stable lights from 1992 to 2012, applying inter-satellite calibration and capping values at 63 while setting values below 6 to zero. It then aggregates the annual calibrated nighttime light values within each postal code boundary using reduceRegion with sum reducer at 1000m scale, and exports a CSV table containing summed NTL values and area for each postal code in Thailand.

Task: Analyze HCHO column density
Analyze the tropospheric formaldehyde (HCHO) column number density over seven geographical regions of Turkey (Marmara, Ege, Akdeniz, Doğu Anadolu, Güneydoğu Anadolu, İç Anadolu, Karadeniz) using Sentinel-5P satellite data for the period April 29 to May 17 in the years 2019, 2020, and 2021. It generates time-series charts showing daily average HCHO levels per year for each region.

Task: Estimate nighttime light intensity per postal code
Calculate calibrated nighttime light intensities for each postal code in Thailand using DMSP-OLS stable lights data from 1992 to 2012. It applies quadratic calibration equations to correct sensor-specific biases, clips values to the valid range [0,63], and aggregates pixel sums within each postal code boundary using reduceRegion. The output is a CSV table exported to Google Drive containing summed calibrated nighttime light values and area for each postal code feature.

Task: Detect land cover change
Detect land cover changes using LandTrendr algorithm applied to Landsat surface reflectance imagery from 1984 to 2019 over a specified area (aoi1, defined by geometry9). It computes a change map based on spectral trajectory analysis of band B5 (shortwave infrared), identifying changes in magnitude and year of detection. The output includes a magnitude of change raster and a year of detection layer visualized with a time-based color palette, alongside reference layers from Landsat 7, Landsat 8, and Sentinel-2 for validation. Additionally, a feature collection 'CAM_2017' is overlaid for comparison, suggesting ground-truth or validation data integration.

Task: Detect land cover change
Detect land cover changes using the LandTrendr algorithm applied to Landsat surface reflectance imagery from 1984 to 2019 over a user-defined area (geometry9). It computes a change map based on spectral trajectory analysis of band B5 (shortwave infrared), identifying changes with specific parameters for magnitude, year of detection, and statistical significance. The outputs include a magnitude of change raster and a year of detection (YOD) layer, both visualized with color palettes, and are clipped to the study area. Additionally, the workflow processes and visualizes multi-temporal Landsat 7, Landsat 8, and Sentinel-2 imagery for 2012–2018 to support change context, and overlays a reference feature collection (CAM_2017) for validation or comparison.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types using Landsat surface reflectance imagery from 2000 to 2020. It merges multiple training feature collections (Degradacion, Deforestacion1, Deforestacion2, NoBosque, Bosque1, NBRegenerado) into a single training dataset, exports it as a FeatureCollection asset, and filters it for samples labeled as land cover class 3. Time-series Landsat 7 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance composites are generated annually, with Band 4 (NIR) from Landsat 7 and Band 5 (NIR) from Landsat 8 extracted, renamed to a common 'T' prefix (e.g., T2000–T2020), and combined into a multiband image stack. The output includes the exported training dataset and a time-series image collection of near-infrared reflectance for classification modeling.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types for the year 1985 using Landsat 5 TOA reflectance data, computing spectral indices (NDVI, MNDWI, SAVI), and applying a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions of interest. The output is a classified land cover map with 13 classes including agriculture, urban areas, wetlands, forests, water bodies, and coastal features, along with accuracy assessment metrics such as confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

Task: Extract NDVI values by season and year
Calculate seasonal and annual mean NDVI values for each feature in a land base polygon collection using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2018 to 2022. It computes NDVI for four quarterly periods (Jan-Mar, Apr-Jun, Jul-Sep, Oct-Dec) and for each full calendar year, then exports the results as a CSV table with feature identifiers and NDVI statistics.

Task: Analyze NDVI temporal changes
Compute and visualizes NDVI composites from Landsat 8 imagery over East Java (Jawa Timur) across eight consecutive 16-day periods between June and October 2020, generating mean NDVI values for the region to assess vegetation dynamics over time.

Task: Extract Landsat imagery for Guatemala
the workflow collects and filters Landsat satellite imagery (from sensors MSS, TM, and ETM+) across multiple missions (Landsat 1–5) over Guatemala for specific time periods. It defines a study area using the country boundary of Guatemala from the LSIB dataset, applies spatial and temporal filtering to each Landsat collection, selects reflective bands (B1–B4), and outputs the filtered image collections for visualization and analysis. The total number of images across all collections is computed and printed. No classification or change detection is performed—only data aggregation and preparation.

Task: Estimate vegetation fraction using MSAVI
Calculate multiple vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, MSAVI, MSAVI_af) from Landsat 5 TOA reflectance data, with a focus on computing fractional vegetation cover (FC) derived from MSAVI_af. It unmasks land cover fractions (urban, vegetation, water, non-photosynthetic vegetation), visualizes various spectral indices, and exports regional mean values of these indices for sample regions, along with exporting the MSAVI image to Google Drive.

Task: Compare land surface changes over time
Analyze changes in the land surface around a specific point in Myanmar using multi-temporal SAR (Sentinel-1) and optical (Sentinel-2, Landsat 8) satellite imagery from February to April 2019. It processes VV-polarized Sentinel-1 GRD data by masking out noisy edges, and applies radiometric scaling to Landsat 8 surface reflectance data. The workflow visualizes pre-, post-, and late-event conditions through RGB composites and single-band VV backscatter layers, enabling qualitative assessment of surface dynamics such as flooding, agricultural activity, or urban change. Outputs include layered visualizations of co-located S1, S2, and L8 images at three time periods for comparative analysis.

Task: Classify land cover in Vichada
Classify land cover in the Vichada department of Colombia using a Random Forest classifier trained on temporal segmentation features derived from Landsat surface reflectance data. It processes four segmented time periods (SG1–SG4), applies masking based on classification confidence, stacks the filtered segments into a multi-band feature image, and performs land cover classification using training samples from 'Entrebamiento_RF_'. The output is a classified land cover map over Vichada, visualized with a specified palette, alongside time-series composites of Landsat bands for validation and context.

Task: Classify agricultural and natural land cover
Classify land cover types in a rural region using Sentinel-2 imagery from mid-2019. It computes median composites for July, August, and September 2019 over a specified geometry, with cloud filtering applied for September. A Random Forest classifier is trained using sample regions from September imagery over a rural area, then applied to the August composite to generate a land cover map. The classification distinguishes four classes: Area Plantio (Agriculture), Solo (Soil), Vegetação Natural (Natural Vegetation), and Agua (Water). The output includes a classified raster map visualized with a legend, exported to Google Drive, and a quantitative area summary per class in hectares and percentages, derived from pixel counts at 30m scale.

Task: Analyze wetland land fraction trends
Calculate the percentage of land cover within HUC-10 watersheds across the Gulf of Mexico region from 1985 to 2019, using annual fractional land images derived from Landsat. It masks areas outside potential wetlands and exports zonal statistics (mean land fraction) per watershed and year to a CSV file.

Task: Map irrecoverable carbon loss from deforestation
the workflow quantifies and maps annual and cumulative losses of irrecoverable carbon (IC) due to deforestation between 2011 and 2019, using ESA land cover change and Hansen forest loss data. It calculates IC loss by masking high-resolution IC data with forest loss years and aggregates results into ecoregions for export as CSV tables.

Task: Classify crop and non-crop areas
Classify agricultural land into crop and non-crop categories using temporal NDVI profiles derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a series of bi-monthly periods from October 2021 to March 2022. It computes NDVI for each period, stacks them into a multi-band image, trains a Random Forest classifier using labeled regions (Crop, Noncrop, water, BU), validates the model accuracy, and exports the classified raster. Additionally, it generates a scatter chart showing mean NDVI trends per class across time and calculates area statistics via masked pixel counting.

Task: Extract NDVI time series for land cover classification
Generate a monthly NDVI time series from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a two-year period (2020–2021) for a specific MGRS tile (32TMK). It applies cloud and shadow masking using the Scene Classification Layer (SCL), computes NDVI, selects the greenest pixel composite per month, and compiles all monthly NDVI images into a multiband stack. This stack is used to perform unsupervised clustering (k-means) for land cover classification and to extract temporal NDVI profiles. Outputs include a classified land cover map, a multiband NDVI stack, individual monthly greenest NDVI mosaics, and a time series chart of mean NDVI per cluster. The results are exported to Google Drive.

Task: Extract daily precipitation accumulation
Extract daily precipitation data from the GPM IMERG dataset for a 30-day period in February–March 2019 over a defined region (karkhe). It filters the NASA/GPM_L3/IMERG_V06 collection day by day, selects the 'IRprecipitation' band, reduces each daily collection to a sum (daily total), renames the band to 'gpm', and combines all 30 daily images into a single multi-band image. The final output is clipped to the karkhe boundary and exported to Google Drive as a raster with 30 bands representing daily precipitation totals.

Task: Process Landsat imagery for land surface analysis
Process Landsat Level-1 TOA reflectance imagery from multiple sensors (Landsat 4–9) over the Aconcagua sub-sub-basin region. It standardizes band names across sensors, applies gain and bias correction using slope and intercept coefficients, performs cloud masking using the CFMask band, and creates a unified, cleaned image collection. The output is a masked and calibrated Landsat surface reflectance dataset mapped over time, intended for downstream land surface analysis such as vegetation or land cover monitoring.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover in a rural area using Sentinel-2 imagery from April 2020 as feature space and training samples collected from a July 2019 image. It applies a Random Forest classifier with 10 trees trained on manually labeled regions to generate a classified land cover map with four classes: Área Plantio, Solo, Vegetação Natural, and Agua. The output includes a classified raster map displayed with a custom color palette, an export to Google Drive, and a legend UI element. Additionally, it computes and prints a summary table of pixel counts, area in hectares, and percentage per class within the study region.

Task: Plot RGB time series
Create interactive RGB time series plots for dynamically defined points or polygons across multiple satellite sensors (MODIS Terra/Aqua, Sentinel-2, Landsat 5/7/8/9). It loads and pre-processes surface reflectance collections—including scaling, cloud masking (using SCL for S2 and QA_PIXEL for Landsat), and band selection—then computes mean pixel values over user-drawn geometries to generate synchronized multi-sensor RGB charts (R: red band, G: green band, B: blue band) with consistent visualization ranges (0.0–0.3). Outputs include an interactive UI with map layers for each sensor at a selected date, real-time coordinate display, polygon drawing/export tools, and stacked time series charts showing temporal evolution of red, green, and blue surface reflectance bands separately per sensor.

Task: Analyze vegetation cover using percentile composites
Generate 20th percentile composite images from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data for wet and dry seasons over Rwanda, focusing on visible bands (B2, B3, B4) to analyze vegetation cover and land surface conditions. Outputs include masked and clipped image composites for both wet and dry periods, visualized using specific reflectance ranges.

Task: Identify land cover change in Horta region
Analyze land cover and land cover change dynamics (loss and gain) between 2017 and 2021 in the Horta agricultural area in the Amazon using precomputed LandTrendr-based classification images. It extracts land cover class, year of detection (YOD) for loss and gain events, clips results to study areas (Horta and counterfactual), generates random sample points within a counterfactual polygon, extracts pixel values at those points, formats coordinates and IDs for CEO (Collect Earth Online) validation, and exports the sample data for ground truthing.

Task: Extract precipitation time series
Extract daily precipitation values at specific point locations using CHIRPS data from 2019 to 2020, computing median values per point per date and returning a feature collection with date-stamped precipitation measurements.

Task: Calculate daily poultry heat stress index
Calculate the daily Heat Stress Index (THI) for poultry (specifically broilers) using meteorological variables derived from GLDAS data for the year 2018. It extracts hourly air temperature, specific humidity, surface pressure, shortwave radiation, and wind speed, aggregates them to daily max, min, and mean values, merges them into a single image collection, computes relative humidity, and applies a series of empirical expressions to derive THIbroilers as the final output. The result is a single mean image of daily THIbroilers over the global land area (excluding masked regions), exported at 25 km resolution.

Task: Estimate water surface area and volume
Calculate daily water surface area or reservoir volume using multiple NDWI-based approaches on Sentinel-2 imagery, applying cloud masking and spatial clipping, with results printed as comma-separated values for each valid image date.

Task: Enhance image radiometry
the workflow enhances the visual appearance of a satellite image by applying min-max normalization using the 2nd and 98th percentile values from each band's distribution, then scaling to 0–255 byte range for improved display contrast. The output is a visually optimized false-color composite (using bands B4, B3, B2) of the input image.

Task: Extract land fraction over time
Extract the percentage of land cover (Perc_Land_Fin) from a custom collection of annual fractional land images derived from Landsat data for the Gulf of Mexico region, spanning from 1984 to 2019, and exports zonal statistics by HUC-10 watershed boundaries as a CSV file.

Create cloud-free mosaics of Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over a glacier study area for multiple dates in 2018, 2019, and 2020. Task: Estimate aquatic vegetation frequency
Estimate the frequency and abundance of aquatic vegetation (AQV) in a coastal region using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2015 to 2021, masked by salinity conditions and land cover unmixing. It computes NDVI and mNDWI indices, applies cloud and standard deviation filtering, and performs spectral unmixing to derive monthly AQV fractions, culminating in a mean AQV map exported as an asset.
